s.t:
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
Protecting Flexport's global operations and assets, enabling secure trade worldwide.

Join Flexport's dynamic Compliance Program as the Senior Manager, Supply Chain Protection & Loss Intelligence. This critical role serves as the single point of accountability for both supply chain protection and loss prevention across Flexport's entire footprint — offices, fulfillment centers, and partner sites worldwide.

The Manager will be responsible for protecting Flexport employees, visitors, assets, and facilities through the design and execution of security programs, while simultaneously driving a proactive loss prevention strategy across the Omni fulfillment network.
Day-to-day, this means managing a team of 50+ contracted security officers across multiple locations, overseeing electronic security infrastructure (CCTV, access control), conducting investigations, and managing the security ticketing system.

Strategically, it means building the analytical foundation to identify loss trends and security gaps before they become incidents, authoring the policies and SOPs that standardize how Flexport protects its people and assets globally, and ensuring every new facility launches with security infrastructure and protocols in place from day one.
You will partner closely with operations, facilities, and leadership to design, implement, and scale security programs for existing and future locations, ensuring our people, assets, and reputation are safeguarded as Flexport rapidly expands into new markets. This is a unique opportunity to build a unified security strategy, moving beyond reactive incident management to a data-driven, proactive approach.

Develop and maintain security and loss prevention metrics, KPIs, and dashboards to measure program effectiveness across all facilities and regions
Analyze incident data to identify trends, loss patterns, root causes, and emerging risks — translating findings into actionable recommendations for leadership
Build reporting frameworks that support data-driven resource allocation, vendor performance evaluation, and security investment decisions
Provide regular analytical reports to senior management on security posture, loss prevention outcomes, and program ROI
Author, maintain, and enforce global security and loss prevention policies, ensuring consistency across all Flexport locations and compliance with local regulatory requirements in each jurisdiction
Develop and implement SOPs for key security scenarios (Active Shooter, Emergency Response, High Value Cage procedures, Product Disposal, etc.)
Create site-level security plans for new and existing facilities, tailored to local risk profiles and operational requirements
Design and deliver training programs across physical security and loss prevention topics (emergency response, office security, travel security, incident reporting, etc.)
Develop audit frameworks and LP checklists for site leads to execute on a recurring basis
Manage physical security programs across all Flexport facilities globally (offices, warehouses, and partner sites), including new locations as Flexport and the Omni fulfillment network expand into new markets
Lead security planning and infrastructure stand-up for new facilities and market entries, including site assessments, vendor selection, and system deployment
Administer and maintain electronic security systems, including CCTV surveillance and access control platforms, and evaluate new technology deployments
Serve as the crisis management coordinator, providing real-time threat assessments and coordinating emergency response across regions
Coordinate with HSE, HR, Legal, and Compliance on cross-functional security and safety matters
Drive loss prevention strategy and investigations for the Omni fulfillment network, including cargo theft, employee theft, unauthorized sellers, workplace violence, and empty package findings
Manage the security and loss prevention ticketing syste, including triaging, updating, and resolving tickets with accurate documentation
Identify root causes of supply chain losses and develop recommendations to reduce future risk
Review, collect, and preserve CCTV evidence to support investigations and legal proceedings
Manage third-party guard services across all locations, including oversight of 50+ security officers, performance tracking, and operational discipline
Manage relationships with security integrators and onboard new vendors as required for geographic expansion
Oversee vendor contracts, MSAs, and NDAs for all security-related service providers
Conduct regular business reviews with key vendors and evaluate service delivery against contractual obligations

8+ years of progressive experience in a rike that combined physical security or loss prevention responsibilities with data analytics, policy development, or program design. Traditional security experience alone is not sufficient — this role requires a candidate who has built metrics programs, authored policies, or used data to drive security strategy.
Demonstrated ability to manage security operations across multiple locations and geographies, including hands-on experience with electronic security systems (CCTV, access control platforms).
Demonstrated experience building and analyzing security and loss prevention metrics, with comfort working in data platforms and translating incident data into actionable insights and executive-level reporting
Proven ability to author global policies, SOPs, security plans, and program documentation from scratch.
Experience managing third-party guard services and security vendor contracts, as well as conducting complex investigations (theft, workplace violence, supply chain security).
Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams including HR, Legal, Operations, and Compliance
An analytical mindset with attention to detail and the ability to identify root causes and solve problems
Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed

The opportunity to build and scale global security and loss prevention programs from the ground up in a rapidly expanding, tech-forward logistics company.
Direct impact on protecting Flexport's people, assets, and reputation across a vast international footprint.

The Finance & Supply Chain Engineering organization includes two complementary teams. Software Engineering builds internal full-stack applications, durable agentic workflows, plugins, MCPs, and measurable AI-enabled engineering practices. Data Engineering builds trusted analytics data assets for Finance and Supply Chain. The teams have distinct charters, with important shared dependencies and broad cross team partnerships across Engineering, Applications, Finance, and Supply Chain.

We are looking for a hands-on senior technical leader who will report alongside the Software Engineering and Data Engineering managers. This is an individual-contributor role with no immediate people-management responsibility.

The Tech Lead will raise the technical bar across both teams, participate in important cross-team or high-risk design decisions, and directly own and ship high-impact work. The role should improve team judgment and autonomy rather than act as a floating architect or universal approval gate.

Partner with the Software Engineering and Data Engineering managers as a peer technical leader; managers retain accountability for people, staffing, priorities, performance, and delivery commitments.
Directly own the architecture, implementation, launch, and operation of one or more high-impact initiatives, remaining accountable for real outcomes rather than advisory output alone.
Guide important design decisions that are cross-team, difficult to reverse, or material to security, financial controls, reliability, data quality, or long-term cost of ownership.
Establish pragmatic engineering standards across architecture, APIs and data contracts, testing, security, reliability, observability, lineage, data quality, and operational ownership.
Advance engineering standards for building with AI, including agentic workflows, evaluation, telemetry, adoption, and outcome measurement.
Work across backend, full-stack, data, and big-data systems, making sound boundary decisions and bringing the right domain experts into the design.
Partner deeply with Engineering, Applications, Product, Finance, Supply Chain, Security, and other stakeholders to translate ambiguous needs into durable technical systems.
Raise the technical capability of both teams through design reviews, code reviews, mentoring, written guidance, and reusable reference implementations.
Protect team autonomy: focus involvement on consequential decisions, clarify principles and tradeoffs, and avoid becoming a required approver for routine or reversible work.

s.h: You might thrive in this role if you
s.t:
Have significant professional engineering experience with sustained staff-level or equivalent impact as an individual contributor; prior people management is not required, but a plus.
Can reason across a full-stack application—from user experience and client architecture through backend services, integrations, authorization, and durable state.
Have strong data-engineering judgment across analytical modeling, batch or streaming pipelines, orchestration, lineage, quality, scale, and downstream data contracts.
Have personally designed, built, shipped, and operated consequential systems, and can go from architecture to implementation details without relying on positional authority.
Have led important technical decisions and cross-team initiatives through influence, clear reasoning, and trusted partnership.
Care deeply about correctness, security, data quality, auditability, operational excellence, and measurable outcomes.
Communicate clearly with engineers, managers, and non-technical partners; lead with context and principles rather than control.

Experience building internal products, developer platforms, workflow systems, or analytics platforms used across multiple teams.
Experience with LLM applications, durable agents, AI evaluations, plugins, MCPs, or measurement of AI-enabled engineering outcomes.
Experience in Finance, Supply Chain, accounting, procurement, ERP, or another domain where controls, reconciliation, and traceability matter.

Als Teil des Tire Supply Chain Management Teams an unserem Standort in Hannover-Stöcken unterstützt du die Synchronisierung des Reifenlogistikprozesses, einschließlich der Koordination des Reifenbaus von den Werken zu den Teststandorten weltweit, mit einem starken Fokus auf Koordination, Optimierung und flexible Problemlösung innerhalb des GTT-RS Teams.

Regelmäßige und effektive Kommunikation mit Lager- und Reifenlogistik, Produktindustrialisierung, GTT und F&E weltweit
Analyse und Optimierung bestehender Prozessketten
KNIME Workflows erstellen zur Automatisierung von wiederkehrenden Tätigkeiten

Erste Erfahrungen in Logistik, Supply Chain Management oder Produktionsplanung sind von Vorteil
Kenntnisse in Datenanalyse-Software (Excel und/oder KNIME)
Sicherer Umgang mit den gängigen MS Office-Programmen
Fließende Deutsch- und sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

Location: 110 Spadina Ave. Unit 200, Toronto, ON, M5V 2K4, Canada

HelloFresh Canada is looking for a strategic and highly analytical Associate Director, Supply Chain Management to act as the central nervous system for our Canadian operations performance.

In this critical individual contributor role, you will be plugged directly across all Canadian Fulfillment teams to deeply understand weekly performance against our business plan and identify the key drivers of any operational gaps.

Serving as the interface between the Canadian business and North American Platforms, you will influence tech and operational prioritization, onboard global best practices, and export Canadian innovations. If you are an expert systems-thinker who thrives on turning complex supply chain metrics into actionable executive strategy, this role is for you.

s.h: Lettuce share what this role will be responsible for
s.t:
Plug directly across all Canadian Operations business units (Procurement, Planning, Logistics, FSQA, and Production) to maintain a holistic, end-to-end view of the supply chain
Monitor weekly operational performance against budget and business plan; proactively diagnose, investigate, and articulate the root causes and key drivers of performance gaps
Serve as the Operations expert and Canadian Commercial business representative for Operations components of the Weekly and Monthly Business Reviews for the Canadian Senior Leadership Team
Serve as the primary interface between the Canadian business and North American Operations Platforms to influence strategic prioritization, alignment, and resource allocation
Supplement HelloFresh Canada’s continuous improvement culture by identifying, onboarding, and implementing international best practices locally, while effectively exporting successful Canadian operational workflows to the broader Operations network.
Organize and secure buy-in from cross-functional stakeholders to drive organizational-level adjustments without direct authority over the teams.
Analyze current business strategies to identify new opportunities for supply chain growth, structural efficiency, or cost savings.

s.h: Sound a-peeling? Here's what we're looking for
s.t:
Undergraduate degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Business, or a highly analytical equivalent field (MBA or specialized technical master's is a bonus).
5+ years of hands-on, progressive experience navigating complex, multi-site distribution networks, physical product scaling, or localized fulfillment operations
Proven track record as a high-impact individual contributor with exceptional relationship and stakeholder management skills; a demonstrated ability to influence, communicate, and partner with cross-functional leaders to drive performance without direct line authority
Experience leading or heavily contributing to executive performance reviews (such as WBRs/MBRs) within a fast-paced corporate or operational framework.
Deep knowledge of supply chain dynamics, data frameworks, and process improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean Six Sigma, workflow automation)
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with advanced operational modeling capabilities to dig into data and pull out clear, concise narratives for the executive team.
Excellent organizational and time management skills
Ability to thrive in an unstructured, fast-paced, and constantly evolving high-growth environment
Able and willing to travel to Canadian distribution centers as required (up to 25%)

s.h: Let’s cut to the cheese, this is why you'll love it here
s.t:

This is a posting for an existing vacancy. We are actively seeking to fill this position.

Founded in 2015, Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software and V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

We are seeking an experienced Staff Logistics Lead to support Shield AI’s X-BAT program within the Aircraft Division. This role will lead the logistics planning, supply support, sustainment analysis, and lifecycle support activities across development, flight test, production, and operational sustainment.
The ideal candidate has strong experience supporting military or defense aviation programs and understands how logistics products, supportability analysis, maintenance planning, and supply chain execution contribute to mission availability and operational readiness. This position requires hands-on experience with Maintenance Task Analysis, Logistics Control Numbers, Reliability and Maintainability artifacts, and Supply Support planning and execution.

Lead logistics and sustainment planning activities for a UAS program across design, production, deployment, and field support phases.
Develop, manage, and maintain integrated logistics support products, including maintenance concepts, support equipment design, provisioning inputs, spares planning, and sustainment documentation.
Perform and manage Maintenance Task Analysis to define preventive and corrective maintenance requirements, task frequencies, required tools, support equipment, skill levels, labor hours, and maintenance levels.
Develop and maintain Logistics Control Number structures to support provisioning, maintenance planning, technical documentation, configuration tracking, and sustainment data management.
Partner with engineering, program management, manufacturing, supply chain, field operations, and customer stakeholders to ensure logistics requirements are incorporated into system design and program execution.
Support Reliability and Maintainability activities, including Level of Repair Analysis, FMECA data analysis, maintainability assessments, corrective action planning, reliability growth inputs, and operational availability improvement initiatives.
Lead supply support activities, including spares analysis, provisioning, parts forecasting, inventory planning, reorder recommendations, repair pipeline coordination, sustainment risk identification, and obsolescence management.
Coordinate with suppliers, depots, repair vendors, and internal teams to ensure timely availability of parts, support equipment, and logistics resources.
Support proposal development, basis of estimate inputs, staffing plans, sustainment strategies, and logistics cost estimates for new and existing UAS programs.
Ensure logistics activities comply with applicable defense standards, contract requirements, export control requirements, and company processes.

Bachelor’s degree in logistics, engineering, supply chain, aviation maintenance, business, or a related field; equivalent military or defense logistics experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
8+ years of experience supporting UAS or fighter aircraft logistics and sustainment
Demonstrated experience with Maintenance Task Analysis and development of maintenance planning data.
Expertise of Logistics Control Number structures and their use in provisioning, maintenance planning, and supportability analysis.
Experience with Reliability and Maintainability principles, including failure modes, maintainability drivers, reliability growth, availability metrics, and field performance analysis, and LORA development
Hands-on supply support experience, including spares planning, provisioning, inventory management, parts forecasting, repairables management, and sustainment execution.
Ability to interpret engineering drawings, bills of material, configuration data, maintenance data, and technical documentation.
Experience working cross-functionally with engineering, program management, supply chain, manufacturing, quality, field service, and customer teams.
Strong analytical, communication, and organizational skills with the ability to lead logistics efforts in a fast-paced program environment.

Proven experience with integrated product support elements, including product support management, supply support, support equipment, manpower and personnel, facilities, maintenance planning,
Experience with provisioning, sparing, or supportability tools such as PowerLOG-J, SLICwave, COMPASS, CASA, OPUS10, EAGLE, or similar systems.
Knowledge of MIL-STD-1388 legacy logistics concepts, GEIA-STD-0007, SAE TA-STD-0017, MIL-HDBK-502A, or related product support standards.
Experience developing logistics inputs for CDRLs, technical manuals, maintenance plans, provisioning data, sparing recommendations, or lifecycle sustainment plans.
Experience with ERP, PLM, or MRP systems such as SAP, Oracle, Costpoint, Teamcenter, Arena, Windchill, or similar platforms.
Active or current security clearance.

About Proton
Join Proton and build a better internet where privacy is the default
Proton was founded in 2014 by scientists from CERN on a simple truth: privacy is a fundamental human right . Since then, we’ve built the world’s largest encrypted email service (Proton Mail) and expanded into Proton VPN, Proton Drive, Proton Pass, and Proton Calendar—tools used by millions globally to protect their freedom, fight censorship, and keep their data safe. In some situations, Proton has literally helped save lives!
We are profitable, independent (no VC control), and selectively hire from the top ~1% of applicants. Our 700+ team members across 50+ countries come from leading organizations and elite academic backgrounds. We move fast, keep hierarchy light, and prioritize impact over optics. If you want to do meaningful work with exceptionally high-caliber people, this is it. Join us and do work you can truly be proud of. Check our open-source projects here !

We are looking for a Procurement Specialist, for our location in Skopje. Your role will be to join the Proton Procurement team, responsible to serve the hardware, networking, and streaming infrastructure of the Proton infrastructure.

As Proton scales up the procurement team is scaling up as well in order to serve the growing demands of the Proton Core and Proton VPN infrastructure teams. You would be part of the team that guarantees Proton's users are going to be served with an optimal and cost-efficient infrastructure.

This includes monitoring potential flaws in servers that are already in use, following up with the infra team, and proactively focusing on establishing the long-term wellbeing of Proton VPN infrastructure.

Together with the Procurement team that is already in place, you will be able to define strategies and create compelling solutions in regard to the demands of the Proton Team.

infrastructure needs

vendors/providers

IT-based background

Interpersonal skills and collaboration with multiple teams, and multiple projects
Good negotiation skills - vital to negotiating vendor contracts
Strong organization and communication skills
Attention to detail and problem-solving skills
Working knowledge of server and data-center hardware: server CPUs (Intel Xeon / AMD EPYC), memory, storage media, RAID, networking gear (switches, NICs, transceivers), and rack
infrastructure — enough to read a spec sheet critically and challenge a vendor
Ability to compare hardware offers on a total-cost basis by sourcing public pricing and creating target pricing

Work that Matters: millions of people trust Proton with their privacy. We answer only to our users — not advertisers, not investors with conflicting agendas, not governments. The work you do here is real, and the impact is measurable. (read more about our impact here )
Stock Options: at Proton, we all have the opportunity to be owners of the company. From day one, you have a real stake in what we're building. When Proton wins, you win.
Technology: you'll get the right hardware and the right software you need to do your best work.
Learning & Development: we invest in your growth because sharp people make us better. Proton is one of the fastest ways to accelerate your career because you'll be thrown into real challenges, with real ownership, from day one.
Employee Benefits: your wellbeing isn't an afterthought. We offer strong health coverage, solid retirement options, generous leave, and wellness support so you can bring your best self to work every day
In-Person Collaboration: Amazing things happen when passionate, smart, and purposeful people get together in the same room. With offices across Geneva, Zürich, Barcelona, London and more, you'll spend most of your time collaborating face-to-face with people who genuinely care about what they're building
Food: Lunch and snacks are on us every day in our offices so you can focus on the work and not on what's for lunch.
Transport: getting to the office shouldn't cost you. We cover public transport, bike allowances, or parking, whichever works for you.
Flexible Working: you own your schedule. Set hours that work for you and your team — because outcomes matter more than when the clock says you started.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
At Proton, we believe diversity drives innovation and strengthens our mission to provide privacy as a default for all. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where all individuals, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, age, sexual orientation, physical ability, or socio-economic background, feel valued and empowered. We strive to create equal opportunities, promote open dialogue, and support continuous learning to ensure every voice is heard and respected.
If you need any extra support or reasonable adjustments during the hiring process, please let your talent partner know.

Location: Melbourne or Sydney, covering ANZ and APAC customers
Employment type: Permanent, full-time
Travel: Interstate and international travel across ANZ and APAC, plus occasional trips for training and to meet RELEX teams in other offices
What we do
RELEX runs the planning decisions behind hundreds of the world's leading retailers and manufacturers, deciding at real scale what gets forecast, stocked, priced, promoted and produced across the value chain. Few problems combine this much data, this much complexity, and this much real-world weight. Get it right and a shelf stays stocked, a factory line keeps moving, and food does not spoil before it is sold. Get it wrong and it shows up in real losses for some of the biggest brands in the world.
We have grown for more than 70 consecutive quarters and we are still accelerating. We are a global team of more than 2,000 people, headquartered in Helsinki, with offices across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific, including Melbourne and Sydney. We are building the next generation of AI-native RELEX implementations across ANZ and APAC, and we are looking for a Supply Chain Consultant to help lead them.

This is a hybrid delivery role. Where traditional projects need separate Business and Solution Consultants, this one combines both in a single practitioner, working alongside customer teams and using AI tooling to accelerate delivery across both disciplines.
It is not a jack-of-all-trades role. It is a force multiplier. You will bring real business and solution consulting depth, plus the AI literacy to do in hours what once took a team of specialists days.

You will run business analysis at strategic, operational and organisational levels, own the design and configuration of RELEX solutions end to end, and act as a trusted advisor to your customer stakeholders. You will also support our sales team with solution positioning, benefit analysis, RFIs and ROI cases.

Drive AI-accelerated delivery - use AI tooling (for example Claude) and prompt engineering daily to speed up documentation, analysis, configuration and stakeholder communication; produce strong first-draft deliverables for expert review; and build reusable prompts, tools and playbooks that lift the whole team, not just your own work.
Business consulting - turn customer objectives into clear requirements, lead process workshops, analyse data and KPIs and present findings to both operational and management audiences, own the backbone of the Solution Design Document, and track KPIs and adoption so the business case is met.
Solution consulting - own and build the solution in RELEX's state-of-the-art configuration UI, standing behind build quality and operational robustness, and train customers to use what you have built.
Act as a trusted advisor - communicate credibly with stakeholders at every level, steer customers to prevent escalations and handle those that arise, and lead executive presentations and value assessments.

s.h: You will thrive here if you
s.t:
Love solving problems and get your energy from a hard one; retail supply chain will keep you busy.
Are curious and always looking for a smarter way, and comfortable saying when something does not make sense.
Enjoy learning fast and want to grow quickly alongside a fast-moving business.
Bring energy and enthusiasm, back your teammates, and share what you learn.
Believe good results and enjoying the work go together, and add to that atmosphere for the people around you.
What you will bring
Some experience in supply chain or retail consulting, solution consulting, or SaaS implementation. Around three years is a good guide, but we care more about how you think than the exact count.
An interest in both sides of delivery: understanding what a customer needs, and helping design and configure the solution that meets it.
Direct work experience or exposure in retail or supply chain, for example grocery, CPG / FMCG, general merchandise, or fashion (or the supplier side).
You already use AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT in your everyday work, and you want to get better at it.
Strong problem-solving skills and curiosity about how supply chain systems work, on both the business and the technical side.
Clear communication, and a knack for explaining something complex simply.
Fluent English, and willing to travel across ANZ and APAC.
A strong plus
Exposure to SQL or another query language.
A STEM degree, or solid retail experience.
A background in consulting, or in building business cases and ROI.
Additional languages, useful across APAC.
Experience working in an international team.
Not sure you tick every box? If this role excites you and you're strong in some of what we've described, we'd still love to hear from you. Tell us what draws you to it.

Flexibility in how and where you work.
Room to grow in a fast-moving, financially strong global company with a strong market position.
Ownership, autonomy and flat hierarchies.
Meaningful work that reduces waste and improves sustainability.
Practical benefits that support work, family, wellbeing and everyday life, plus annual leave and two paid volunteering days a year.
An international career with real learning and development opportunities.
Apply
We are a global community of different cultures, voices and experiences, and we hire for capability and potential. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and use inclusive, gender-neutral language throughout our hiring.
To be considered you will need to be based in Melbourne or Sydney and hold valid Australian work rights. Apply with your CV and a short cover letter. Be part of the future. Be RELEX.

About Halter
At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences.

Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance.

Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .
To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram .
We’re looking for an experienced Senior Talent Specialist to join our People and Culture team. This is a great role for someone who’s passionate about finding great talent and working across various markets. We fundamentally believe the biggest driver of company success will be the speed and quality of our hiring. It sets the foundation for everything else that we do to achieve our ambitious mission.

As a key member of the People & Performance team, you’ll play a hands-on role in attracting, sourcing, and hiring world-class talent to support our business as we scale globally. You’ll work closely with hiring managers to understand their team needs, anticipate upcoming roles, and manage end-to-end recruitment processes that ensure we bring in exceptional people who align with our mission and values.
Reporting to the Talent Lead, you’ll focus on executing recruitment strategies, managing candidate pipelines, and delivering an outstanding candidate experience that reflects the calibre of our product and culture. This role is perfect for someone who thrives in a fast-moving environment, enjoys partnering closely with teams across the business, and wants to have a direct impact on how we grow.

s.h: What your day will look like
s.t:
Manage full-cycle recruitment for roles across regions and functions, from sourcing and screening to coordinating interviews and supporting offer processes.
Contribute to talent strategy and workforce planning, supporting forward-looking hiring plans, capability mapping, and future skill needs as the business scales.
Help shape and evolve our Employee Value Proposition (EVP), partnering with People & Performance and the business to ensure our story resonates in the market and reflects the real employee experience.
Build scalable recruitment practices and foundations, designing processes, tools, and ways of working that can flex across regions, functions, and increasing hiring volumes.
Upskill and enable hiring leaders, through coaching, training, and ongoing partnership to lift interviewing quality, assessment rigour, and hiring decision-making.
Support compensation benchmarking and market insights, contributing data and insights to inform fair, competitive, and consistent offers aligned to our compensation philosophy.
Partner on diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives, helping embed inclusive hiring practices and broaden access to talent across all roles.
Represent Halter in the market, acting as an ambassador at events, universities, and industry forums to strengthen our talent brand.
Build and maintain strong candidate pipelines for current and future roles, proactively sourcing talent through multiple channels.
Work closely with hiring managers to understand role requirements, team goals, and key success profiles.
Provide guidance on hiring processes and help managers run smooth, effective, and inclusive recruitment cycles.
Deliver an exceptional, consistent candidate experience at every stage of the process, reflecting our culture and values.
Ensure all communication and interactions contribute positively to our employer brand.
Maintain our ATS and recruitment workflows to keep the hiring process efficient and organised.
Track and share key metrics like time-to-fill, pipeline progress, and candidate feedback to help improve our approach over time.
Support initiatives around internal mobility, diversity, and employer branding.
Look for opportunities to improve recruitment processes and tools as we scale.We’re a fast-moving growth company, so from time to time, other responsibilities will pop up and you’ll be part of making it all happen!

5+ years' experience in Talent Acquisition, ideally within high-growth or global technology environments, recruiting across multiple disciplines. Experience hiring for Supply Chain, Logistics, or other technical functions is highly desirable.
Proven experience building and scaling high-performing teams across multiple regions.
Strategic business partner who can zoom in and out: from exec-level reporting to day-to-day hiring excellence.
Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, a true business partner to hiring teams.
Demonstrated success working in a fast-paced, high-volume hiring environment without compromising on the quality of talent we bring through the door.
You’ll have a deep knowledge of sourcing techniques and channels, and know what it takes to seek out the best talent globally.
Strong reporting and data skills; you’re able to track, analyse, and present key hiring metrics where needed.
Familiarity with employment laws, immigration requirements, and compliance across New Zealand and ideally Australia too.
High emotional intelligence with excellent communication skills; a proactive, solutions-focused self-starter who thrives in ambiguity and takes strong ownership and accountability.
Our Office First Approach
There’s a reason you visit your friends in person, live with your family and don’t do dinners over Zoom. Humans are wired for connection. We believe a world-class, in-person office culture is the best way for high-performing teams.
Being office first is a core pillar of our culture. We believe in-person connections are key to driving your own growth, learning, impact, and building genuine long-lasting relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful and aligned work. We don’t like having heaps of rules or policies, but this means having strong, trusted relationships is critical.
We’re office first , not office only . This means working from the office everyday is our default setting, but we flex when we need to. We have a high-trust culture, so everyone is trusted to do what’s best for Halter.
Our office vibe is something special, it’s hard to describe until you’re here, but people at Halter who have come from fully remote or hybrid companies say they could never go back - the high energy and spectacular people they are now surrounded by everyday makes work so enjoyable. Your growth, your learning and your impact is truly unlimited here, and a big part of that comes from being together solving problems, innovating, building context, and constantly learning from each other.

Votre mission
Rattaché(e) à la Direction Générale, vous pilotez l'ensemble de l'organisation Supply Chain du marché, comprenant les activités de Planification de la demande (Market Planning) , Distribution (Market Distribution) et Service Clients / Gestion des commandes (Customer Order Desk) . À ce titre, vous garantissez la disponibilité des pneumatiques, le respect des niveaux de service clients et l'optimisation des flux logistiques, conformément à la stratégie de l'entreprise et aux exigences du marché.
Vos principales responsabilités
Management et pilotage de la Supply Chain
Encadrer et développer les équipes Planning, Distribution et Service Clients.
Assurer l'amélioration continue des processus Supply Chain et coordonner les évolutions avec les fonctions centrales.
Garantir une collaboration efficace entre les équipes marché et les sites de production.
Piloter les indicateurs de performance et mettre en œuvre les plans d'actions nécessaires.
Planification de la demande
Élaborer et maintenir des prévisions de ventes glissantes à 18 mois en tenant compte de la stratégie de l'entreprise, des besoins clients et des évolutions du marché.
Garantir la disponibilité des produits conformément aux niveaux de service définis.
Analyser les performances commerciales et les tendances du marché afin d'optimiser les prévisions.
Piloter les processus de lancement et de retrait de produits.
Assurer le suivi de la fiabilité des prévisions et mener les actions correctives nécessaires.
Veiller à l'approbation mensuelle des prévisions en collaboration avec les équipes Ventes, Contrôle de gestion, Pricing et Direction.
Maintenir les paramètres Supply Chain dans les systèmes d'information (stock de sécurité, tailles de lots, règles de réapprovisionnement, etc.).
S'assurer du respect de la politique de prévisions par les équipes commerciales.
Distribution et logistique
Organiser la distribution des produits depuis les centres de distribution régionaux dans le respect des attentes clients, des contraintes opérationnelles et des objectifs de coûts.
Garantir la qualité des prestations logistiques conformément aux standards du Groupe.
Piloter les relations contractuelles avec les prestataires logistiques et transporteurs.
Assurer le suivi des performances logistiques : entreposage, transport, gestion des créneaux de livraison et qualité de service.
Gestion des commandes clients
Garantir l'efficacité et la qualité du traitement des commandes conformément aux procédures de l'entreprise.
Veiller au respect des exigences légales et réglementaires dans le traitement des commandes.
Organiser et sécuriser les livraisons directes usine-client.
Maintenir un portefeuille de commandes fiable et à jour afin d'assurer une exécution optimale.
Gestion des stocks
Assurer le suivi continu et l'optimisation des niveaux de stock.
Analyser les flux entrants et sortants, les taux de rotation, les couvertures de stock et les capacités de stockage.
Optimiser la structure des stocks en fonction des catégories de produits et des marques.
Mettre en œuvre une politique de stocks saine afin d'anticiper les risques d'obsolescence et de favoriser l'écoulement des produits à faible rotation.
Contribution stratégique
Déployer la stratégie de niveau de service définie au niveau régional et européen.
Développer des solutions logistiques innovantes pour améliorer la satisfaction client et la performance opérationnelle.
Participer à l'exécution des projets stratégiques de l'entreprise.
Contribuer aux démarches qualité et à la transformation de la Supply Chain.

Reporting directly to the General Management, you will lead the entire Market Supply Chain organization, including Demand Planning (Market Planning), Distribution (Market Distribution), and Customer Service / Order Management (Customer Order Desk).
In this role, you will ensure tire availability, maintain customer service levels, and optimize logistics flows in line with the company's strategy and market requirements.

Supply Chain Management and Leadership
Lead, coach, and develop the Planning, Distribution, and Customer Service teams.
Drive continuous improvement of Supply Chain processes and coordinate developments with central functions.
Ensure effective collaboration between market teams and production plants.
Monitor Supply Chain performance indicators and implement corrective action plans when necessary.
Demand Planning
Develop and maintain an 18-month rolling sales forecast, taking into account the company's strategy, customer requirements, and market developments.
Ensure product availability in line with agreed service levels.
Analyze sales performance and market trends to optimize demand forecasts.
Manage product launch and phase-out processes.
Monitor forecast accuracy and implement corrective actions as required.
Ensure monthly forecast alignment and approval in collaboration with Sales, Controlling, Pricing, and Management teams.
Maintain Supply Chain parameters within information systems (safety stock, batch sizes, replenishment rules, etc.).
Ensure compliance with forecasting policies across the Sales organization.
Distribution and Logistics
Organize product distribution from regional distribution centers while balancing customer expectations, operational constraints, and cost objectives.
Ensure logistics service quality in accordance with Group standards.
Manage contractual relationships with logistics providers and carriers.
Monitor logistics performance, including warehousing, transportation, delivery scheduling, and service quality.
Customer Order Management
Ensure efficient and high-quality order processing in compliance with company procedures.
Ensure adherence to all legal and regulatory requirements related to order processing.
Organize and secure direct factory-to-customer deliveries.
Maintain a reliable and up-to-date order portfolio to ensure optimal execution.
Inventory Management
Continuously monitor and optimize inventory levels.
Analyze inbound and outbound flows, inventory turnover, stock coverage, and storage capacities.
Optimize inventory structure across product categories and brands.
Implement sound inventory management practices to anticipate obsolescence risks and promote the sell-through of slow-moving products.
Strategic Contribution
Deploy the service level strategy defined at regional and European levels.
Develop innovative logistics solutions to enhance customer satisfaction and operational performance.
Contribute to the execution of the company's strategic projects.
Support quality initiatives and Supply Chain transformation programs.
Formation
Bac+5 (Master, école de commerce, école d'ingénieurs ou équivalent) avec une spécialisation en Supply Chain, Logistique, Transport ou Gestion des opérations.
Expérience
Expérience significative de 5 à 10 ans dans des fonctions Supply Chain, Logistique, Distribution ou Demand Planning.
Expérience réussie dans le pilotage de processus logistiques complexes et dans la gestion de prestataires externes.
Bonne maîtrise des processus commerciaux et de la gestion de la qualité.

The Manager, International Customer Supply Chain will play a key role in delivering an exceptional customer and retail partner experience across rhode’s growing international business.

This role will partner closely with Sales, Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Finance, Operations, international distributors and retail partners to ensure strong execution across order management, inventory flow, launch planning, and ongoing customer supply chain performance.

This role will support multiple international markets and distribution partners, requiring strong coordination across regions and global supply chain processes.

Über tonies: tonies ist die weltweit führende interaktive Audioplattform für Kinder mit mehr als 10 Millionen verkauften Tonieboxen und 125 Millionen verkauften Tonies.

Das intuitive und preisgekrönte Audiosystem hat mit seinem kindersicheren, kabellosen und bildschirmfreien Ansatz die Art und Weise verändert, wie junge Kinder selbstständig spielen und lernen. Tonieboxen wurden bereits in über 100 Ländern aktiviert, und das Content-Portfolio umfasst rund 1.400 Tonies in mehreren Sprachen.

Seit der Gründung hat tonies bedeutende Meilensteine erreicht, darunter den Börsengang an der Frankfurter Wertpapierbörse im November 2021 sowie den Aufbau eines weltweit präsenten Teams von über 550 engagierten Fachkräften, die in verschiedenen Ländern tätig sind.
Teil unseres tonies-Teams zu werden bedeutet, an einer inspirierenden Mission teilzuhaben: innovative und bedeutungsvolle Erlebnisse für Kinder auf der ganzen Welt zu schaffen. Gemeinsam gestalten wir die Zukunft des Spielens, Lernens und der Fantasie.
Du als Teil von tonies: Bei tonies bist du nicht einfach nur eine „studentische Hilfskraft“ – du bist ein voll integriertes Teammitglied. Du erhältst tiefe Einblicke in die Supply Chain einer schnell wachsenden, globalen Marke und bekommst die Möglichkeit selbst echte Verantwortung zu übernehmen.
Während andere vielleicht von wachsenden To-Do-Listen überwältigt werden, behältst du einen kühlen Kopf und konzentrierst dich auf das Wesentliche. Du blühst auf, wenn es darum geht, komplexe Probleme in einem globalen, dynamischen Umfeld zu lösen, das durch flache Hierarchien und agile Entscheidungsfindung geprägt ist.
Deine Aufgaben umfassen: Operative Unterstützung: Unterstützung des Global Supply Planning-Teams bei der Nachverfolgung internationaler Lieferungen von unseren Lieferanten zu den lokalen Lagern, Gewährleistung einer termingerechten und präzisen Durchführung von ERP-Transaktionen, Überwachung von Lagerbeständen sowie die Analyse und Optimierung von Kernprozessen der Lieferkette.
Datenmanagement: Unterstützung bei der Zusammenstellung und Aufbereitung kritischer Datensätze, die als Grundlage für präzise Bedarfs-, Liefer- und Bestandsprognosen dienen.
Systeme & Administration: Pflege und Optimierung unseres ERP-Systems sowie Abwicklung allgemeiner kaufmännischer Aktivitäten innerhalb der Lieferplanung und des operativen Einkaufs.
Reporting & Analytics: Erstellung umfassender Berichte, Verknüpfung verschiedener Datensätze sowie Unterstützung bei der Nachverfolgung von KPIs und der Prozessdokumentation.
Abteilungsübergreifende Zusammenarbeit: Unterstützung des Teams an den Schnittstellen zu anderen Abteilungen, um einen reibungslosen Ablauf der Supply-Chain-Aktivitäten zu gewährleisten.
Was wir uns von dir wünschen: Ausbildung/Studium: Du bist derzeit in einem Studiengang der Betriebswirtschaftslehre (BWL), des Supply Chain Managements, der Logistik, des Wirtschaftsingenieurwesens oder eines verwandten Bereichs immatrikuliert.
Berufliche Fähigkeiten: Erste Erfahrungen durch Praktika oder Werkstudententätigkeiten in einem Unternehmensumfeld sind von Vorteil.
Kommunikation: Fließende Kommunikationsfähigkeiten sowohl in Deutsch (C1) als auch in Englisch (B2) sind erforderlich. Ein sicheres Auftreten und eine kooperative, teamorientierte Denkweise runden dein Profil ab.
Analytische Denkweise: Es macht dir Spaß, komplexe Informationen logisch zu strukturieren und klar zu präsentieren. Du arbeitest mit hoher Präzision und Gewissenhaftigkeit.
IT-Kenntnisse: Du bist ein fortgeschrittener Anwender von MS Office (insbesondere Excel) und bringst eine natürliche Neugier für das Erlernen neuer IT-Umgebungen und ERP-Systeme mit.
Selbstmanagement: Du bist ein proaktiver Selbststarter mit exzellentem Zeitmanagement und der Fähigkeit, dich schnell an neue Anforderungen anzupassen.
Warum tonies? Globales Teamwork: Wir arbeiten über Abteilungs- und Ländergrenzen hinweg an unserer Vision, die Toniebox in jedes Kinderzimmer der Welt zu bringen.
Come as you are: Das gilt nicht nur für den Dresscode, sondern auch für alles andere. Denn nur dort, wo man sich wirklich wohlfühlt, kann man sein Bestes geben.
Erholung & Freizeit: Genieße 20 Tage bezahlten Jahresurlaub (basierend auf einer 5-Tage-Woche) sowie drei zusätzliche freie Tage (Rosenmontag, Heiligabend und Silvester).
Sprachenlernen & Entspannung: Verbessere deine Kommunikationsfähigkeiten mit der Sprachlern-App Babbel und finde Entspannung durch unseren Zugang zur Meditations-App Calm.
Rabatte: Profitiere von attraktiven Rabatten auf unser gesamtes tonies-Produktsortiment.
Gut zu wissen: Als Teil unserer Grundsätze setzen wir uns aktiv für Inklusion und Vielfalt bei tonies ein. Wir schätzen und feiern die unterschiedlichen Fähigkeiten, ethnischen Zugehörigkeiten, Glaubensrichtungen und Geschlechter unserer Kolleginnen und Kollegen. Jede*r ist herzlich willkommen und wird in jeder Phase der gemeinsamen Reise in seiner/ihrer Entwicklung unterstützt.
Wir freuen uns darauf, von dir zu hören!

About Halter
At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences.

Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance.

Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .
To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram .

Halter builds hardware that works in some of the most demanding environments on earth. The quality of what we ship matters enormously, to the farmers who depend on it every day and to the mission we're on. As we scale into multiple products and higher volumes, we need someone to own quality across the full supply chain and build it into a genuine competitive advantage.
The Director of Supply Chain Quality owns Halter's end-to-end quality function, based at our Auckland HQ. You'll lead two teams: a Supplier Quality team that owns quality at our component suppliers from pre-selection auditing through to ongoing part approval, and a Contract Manufacturing Quality team that owns incoming, in-process, and outgoing quality at our contract manufacturers. Together they form a quality system with clear accountability and no gaps.
A critical part of this role is owning Halter's quality assurance specifications, developed and maintained in collaboration with the Supplier Quality team, the Contract Manufacturing Quality team, and the hardware design team. These specs are the backbone of the quality system. Getting them right and keeping them current is what makes everything else work.
You'll set the quality strategy, develop your team leaders and their teams, own the quality framework across the supply chain, and be the escalation point when quality issues arise at the boundary between supplier and CM. You'll work closely with hardware engineering, operations, and sourcing to ensure quality is designed in and not just inspected for.
This is not a documentation role. The best quality leaders get into the detail. They visit suppliers, they walk the production line, they dig into the data behind a failure mode, and they develop a sharp instinct for what actually drives quality outcomes versus what just adds paperwork. We want someone who is technically curious, comfortable getting their hands dirty, and able to distinguish between a process that genuinely improves quality and one that exists to say it exists.
You'll be measured on product quality, supplier and CM quality performance, and your ability to build a quality function that scales with Halter's growth.

Leadership and Team Development
Lead and develop the Supplier Quality and Contract Manufacturing Quality teams, setting clear direction, holding a high bar, and developing strong people in both functions.
Build the culture of the quality function: rigorous, fast-moving, low bureaucracy, and deeply connected to the engineering and operations teams.
Set clear accountability between the two teams and own the interface between them, ensuring the handoff between supplier OQC and CM IQC is well-governed and issues at the boundary are resolved quickly.
Quality Assurance Specifications
Own the development and ongoing maintenance of Halter's quality assurance specifications, working across the Supplier Quality team, the Contract Manufacturing Quality team, and the hardware design team to ensure specs reflect current design intent and are correctly implemented across the supply chain.
Ensure QA specs are the single source of truth for what quality standards are required at suppliers and at our CMs, and that they are kept current as products evolve.
Define the governance model for how QA specs are reviewed, approved, and updated, and ensure all three teams are aligned on the process.
Quality Strategy and Systems
Own Halter's quality management system across the supply chain, ensuring it is fit for purpose, consistently applied, and evolves as the business scales.
Build the quality metrics and reporting that give leadership a clear and honest picture of quality performance across suppliers and contract manufacturers.
Lead root cause analysis and corrective action on significant quality escapes, ensuring lessons are captured and systemic issues are fixed rather than managed.
Collaborate with the Operations Delivery Lead and Head of Supply Chain Strategy to ensure quality risks are visible early in NPI programmes and sustaining activities.

Significant experience leading quality functions in a hardware or electronics manufacturing environment, ideally spanning both supplier quality and manufacturing quality.
Experience owning quality assurance specifications and the cross-functional process of developing and maintaining them alongside engineering and operations teams.
A track record of building and developing high-performing quality teams, with the credibility to set a high bar and the people skills to bring others with you.
Deep understanding of quality management systems, audit methodologies, part approval processes, and how to apply them pragmatically in a fast-moving environment.
Strong cross-functional leadership across engineering, operations, and sourcing teams.
Analytically sharp and data-driven. You use quality data to drive systemic improvement, not just to track defects.
Technically hands-on. You're not afraid to get into the detail of a process, a specification, or a production line to understand what's really driving quality. You can distinguish between a quality process that genuinely moves the needle and one that exists to tick a box.
Clear, direct communication at every level. You can give a board-level quality update and a detailed corrective action review.
Low ego and comfortable with discomfort. You lean into hard conversations, raise the awkward thing early, and never shy away from tension when it needs to be resolved.
You're fun and a joy to work with. Quality work is demanding and detail-intensive. You bring energy, rigour, and optimism to it, and people are better for having you around.

Rocket Lab’s Supply Chain team is responsible for the flow of all materials, products, and components throughout the business. With many of our own products functioning as critical components to our own and our customers’ missions, the Supply Chain team has a direct impact on the success of our rocket and satellite programs.

They set up assembly kits that enable our technicians to put together our Electron rockets, manage inventory, look after shipping and receiving, manage direct and indirect procurement, and inspect and ensure that all of our materials and products are compliant and up to standard.

They are the chain that links our teams together and are critical to our success.

Based on site at Rocket Lab’s Middle River, MD production facility, the Senior Logistics Coordinator is responsible for domestic and international shipping.

There are hundreds of components that are used to manufacture Electron’s Launch Vehicle that are globally sourced and/or moved domestically and internationally between Rocket Lab manufacturing sites. This role will actively manage the logistical movements of these items.

This role is responsible for managing domestic and international logistics from suppliers, between Rocket Lab locations internationally and beyond. The role also requires adherence to ITAR and other applicable export regulations.

Train, and support logistics staff to meet performance goals.

Track and analyze logistics KPIs and prepare performance reports.
Develop and implement risk management and contingency plans for disruptions.

High school diploma and 2+ years of experience.
Exposure to international shipping regulations.

International Air Transportation Association, (IATA) / International Maritime Dangerous Good (IMDG) knowledge.
Strong IT knowledge, comfortable working with Windows.
Experience working with a fully integrated Enterprise Resource Planning system.
Basic understanding of necessary documentation for international shipping.

The NPI Prototype Procurement Manager owns fast-turn prototype sourcing during new product development. When engineering needs a part quoted and built in days, not weeks, this role makes it happen, and makes sure the part we source for a prototype build doesn't quietly become a bad default for production.
This role reports to the Director of Supply Chain and works closely with engineering, our prototype contract manufacturers, and our production sourcing team. Prototype CMs are good at turning parts fast; they are not set up to decide which of those parts should become a real production supplier, or to catch when a rushed sourcing decision is costing us on markup or quality risk down the line. That decision needs a dedicated owner on our side.
We are building this role now because the gap is already showing up in real costs: parts moving slower than they should, and markups on prototype-CM-sourced parts that we're paying today without anyone tracking whether that's the right long-term call.
Scope
Fast-turn sourcing: for parts that are strategic, long-lead, or clearly headed toward production, you run the RFQ and sourcing decision directly rather than letting a prototype CM default-source it under time pressure.
Prototype-to-production tracking: for parts a prototype CM sources on our behalf, you track what was bought, from whom, and at what cost, and you flag early which of those should transition to a qualified production supplier instead of carrying forward by default.
Cost visibility: you own should-cost tracking on new parts as designs stabilize, flagging anything trending over target early enough to actually do something about it.
This role sits specifically in the handoff between early prototype builds and production. Production commodity strategy, supplier negotiation, and cost-out on qualified production parts stay with our sourcing team. Day-to-day material tracking and expediting once a part is in production stays with our materials team. This role owns the messy middle: prototype-stage sourcing decisions that determine what production inherits.
This role starts as an individual contributor working in close partnership with engineering.
Who this role is for
You have direct experience sourcing prototype and early-production parts in a hardware environment, working shoulder to shoulder with engineering while designs are still moving. You're comfortable quoting and placing an order on a part that might change again next week.
You think past the next build. When a prototype shop sources a part fast, you're the person asking whether that supplier, that price, and that quality level are good enough to carry into production, or whether it needs to change before it's too late to change cheaply.
You're comfortable working through and around a contract manufacturer's own sourcing team rather than owning a factory floor yourself. You know how to get a CM's buyer to move fast for you, and you know when to route around them and source directly.
You have a cost-conscious streak. You notice when a markup looks high and you're willing to do the work to find out if it's justified.
You are comfortable in early-stage environments where the playbook is still being written, and where this specific handoff between prototype and production sourcing hasn't had a dedicated owner before.
This role is not a fit for
You are looking to own production commodity strategy or long-term supplier negotiation. That sits with our sourcing team.
You are looking to own day-to-day material tracking and expediting once parts are in production. That sits with our materials team.
You need stable designs and a locked BOM to work effectively. This role lives in the period before that’s true.
You would find a startup operating tempo frustrating.

Prototype sourcing
Run quick-turn RFQs and place orders directly for strategic, long-lead, or clearly production-bound parts during prototype builds.
Partner with engineering embedded in design reviews and build planning, understanding what’s changing and what’s stabilizing.
Manage supplier relationships for quick-turn shops separate from our production supplier base.
Prototype-to-production handoff
Track every part sourced by a prototype CM on our behalf: supplier, cost, and whether it’s fit to carry forward.
Flag parts that should transition to a qualified production supplier early enough to make the change before it’s expensive.
Hand off qualified parts and supplier context cleanly to our production sourcing team, with a clear paper trail rather than tribal knowledge.
Cost visibility
Own should-cost tracking on new parts as designs stabilize, flagging cost overruns early.
Identify where prototype CM markups are worth the convenience and where a direct sourcing decision would save real money.
Cross-functional partnership
Partner with our production sourcing team on the handoff for parts moving from prototype to production.
Partner with our materials team on build timing and part availability during prototype phases.
Partner with engineering on design-for-sourcing input while parts are still changeable.

4+ years in procurement or sourcing supporting new product development in a hardware or industrial product environment.
Direct experience with fast-turn/quick-turn sourcing (rapid prototyping shops, quick-turn machining or fab, low-volume electronics).
Comfort working alongside a contract manufacturer’s own sourcing team rather than owning a factory floor directly.
Experience evaluating whether a prototype-sourced part or supplier is fit to carry into production.
Ability to operate independently and build process where none exists yet.

Experience in battery, energy storage, power electronics, or other hardware-adjacent categories.
Should-cost or cost estimation experience on early-stage or immature designs.
Experience transitioning parts from a prototype or contract manufacturer to a qualified production supplier.
Early-stage startup experience.

Enpal macht das möglich mit einer integrierten Gesamtlösung für dezentrale Energie – von Solaranlage und Batteriespeicher über Wallbox, Smart Meter bis zur Wärmepumpe. Herzstück ist unsere KI-gestützte Plattform Enpal.One +, die tausende Systeme intelligent vernetzt und Strombezug sowie -einspeisung effizient am Energiemarkt optimiert.
Bist Du bereit für Lösungen, die mehr als nur ein Versprechen sind und täglich echte Lebensqualität in tausende Haushalte bringen? Was du bei Enpal gestaltest, liefert morgen sauberen Strom und verändert nachhaltig, wie wir Energie nutzen.
Deine Aufgaben
Du gestaltest und entwickelst strategische Initiativen im Supply Chain Management zur Skalierung, Effizienzsteigerung und Professionalisierung der Organisation.
Entwicklung von Konzepten zur Optimierung von Einkaufs-, Logistik- und SCM-Prozessen sowie zur Erschließung neuer Wertschöpfungspotenziale entlang der Lieferkette.
Du unterstützt die digitale Transformation im SCM voran und identifizierst Anwendungsfälle für Automatisierung, Advanced Analytics und KI.
Leitung und Koordination cross-funktionaler Projekte gemeinsam mit Einkauf, Logistik, Fulfillment, Finance, Tech und weiteren Fachbereichen.
Du analysierst geschäftskritische Herausforderungen, entwickelst datenbasierte Lösungen und leitest konkrete Maßnahmen mit messbarem Business Impact ab.
Du arbeitest eng mit Technologie- und Produktteams zusammen, um skalierbare Prozesse, Systeme und Strukturen für die SCM-Organisation zu schaffen.
Dein Profil
1+ Jahre Erfahrung in einem analytischen oder strategischen, dynamischen Umfeld, z. B. Strategieberatung oder Scale-up.
Hohe strategische Denkschärfe, ausgeprägte Problemlösungskompetenz und die Fähigkeit, komplexe Fragestellungen strukturiert zu bearbeiten.
Nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Leitung komplexer, cross-funktionaler Projekte in dynamischen Organisationen.
Stark ausgeprägtes Stakeholder-Management sowie Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Führungskräften und relevanten Entscheidern.
Unternehmerische Denkweise, Ownership, ein Blick für Skalierung und Freude an Transformations- und Wachstumsprojekten.
Starkes Interesse an Supply Chain Management, Einkauf, Logistik sowie an Technologie, Digitalisierung und KI.
Du bist interessiert, auch wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen erfüllst? Bewirb dich trotzdem! Wir freuen uns darauf, dein Potenzial zu entdecken - unabhängig davon, ob deine Erfahrung jede einzelne Voraussetzung erfüllt. ☀️
Darauf kannst Du Dich freuen
Arbeite in Deutschlands erstem grünen Unicorn - Gestalte aktiv die solare Energiewende mit.
Die Sonne scheint auf der ganzen Welt - Bei Enpal arbeitest du mit einem hochmotivierten, diversen Team aus über 65 Nationalitäten.
Das ideale Setup für deinen Fokus - Wir sind überzeugt, dass exzellente Ergebnisse dort entstehen, wo die Bedingungen stimmen. Deshalb setzen wir auf ein hybrides Arbeitskonzept, das dir die Freiheit gibt, immer genau so zu arbeiten, wie es am besten zu deinen Aufgaben passt. Du brauchst neue Impulse auf internationalem Niveau? Mit Workflex bieten wir, abhängig von deiner Verantwortung, die Möglichkeit, deine Tätigkeit bis zu 30 Tage im Jahr ins Ausland zu verlegen.
Grown-up Business & Startup Spirit - In unserem modernen Office in Berlin-Friedrichshain findest du von höhenverstellbaren Tischen, Tischtennisplatte bis gefüllten Getränkekühlschränken und Barista-Coffee alles was das Herz begehrt.
Dein Kick-start bei Enpal - Onboarding-Tag mit Welcome Bag, Buddy-Programm und einem Team, das dich wirklich abholt.
Bleib auf dem Laufenden & gestalte mit - Transparente All-Hands, kurze Entscheidungswege und eine offene Feedback-Kultur, denn ohne Fehler gibt es keinen Fortschritt.
Energiewende geht nur gemeinsam - Bei Enpal erwartet dich ein legendärer Teamspirit und unvergessliche Team- und Companyevents.
Dein Extra-Boost - 29 + 2 Urlaubstage, vergünstigte Mitgliedschaft bei Wellhub und Corporate Benefits. Alles, was dir hilft, Arbeit und Leben gut zu verbinden.
Wir bei Enpal sind stolz auf die Vielfältigkeit unseres Teams. Weder bei der Einstellung noch während des Beschäftigungsverhältnisses werden Entscheidungen auf Basis von Hautfarbe, Religion oder religiösen Glaubens, ethnischer oder nationaler Herkunft, Nationalität, Geschlechteridentität, sexuelle Orientierung, Behinderung oder Alter getroffen. Enpal steht für einen sicheren Arbeitsplatz und geht gegen Diskriminierung und Belästigung jeglicher Art vor.

This is Procurement at Lattice
Lattice’s Procurement Team builds value for the company through both supplier and stakeholder relationships and balanced agreements. As part of the accounting team, we place a large focus on risk mitigation and compliance in addition to the commercial elements of the deals we support. We are a small team with a huge impact on Lattice’s future success.
Contract details: This is a two-month contract role, fully remote, 3 days/week guaranteed with the potential for additional hours as needed. You’ll have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience with the full procurement lifecycle, procurement orchestration tools (P2P), and exposure to a high-performing tech organization.

You’ll be responsible for reviewing, scoping, negotiating, and executing procurement requests from intake through signature.
You’ll partner with cross-functional leaders, stakeholders, and department contacts from FP&A, Finance, IT, Security, Compliance, Privacy, and Legal to ensure our deals meet or exceed team requirements.
You’ll provide consultation before, during, and after deal cycles to our internal teams, ensuring that we purchase the right things and get exceptional value from our suppliers and partners.
What You Will Bring to the Table
3 years of experience with commercial negotiations, procurement initiatives, or complex vendor engagements.
A strong understanding of SaaS procurement, services agreements, and supplier relationships, along with hands-on experience using procurement orchestration tools, ideally Zip.
Strong attention to detail to ensure clean and accurate records within Lattice systems reflecting up-to-date deal statuses, vendor records, and intake reviews.
Clear, thoughtful communication skills, with the ability to adapt your approach based on audience and situation.

Presales Solution Principal — Pricing & Promotions
RELEX Solutions offers an AI-native, unified supply chain and retail planning platform that helps retailers, wholesalers, manufacturers, and consumer packaged goods (CPG) companies plan, optimize, and automate operations across demand forecasting, inventory, merchandising, pricing, and supply chain management.
The Presales Solution Principal at RELEX is a pivotal strategic role that enhances the sales team's effectiveness throughout the sales cycle. This position combines expertise in sales strategy, subject matter knowledge, process facilitation, and execution.
This role supports RELEX's Pricing & Promotions solutions, including price optimization, promotion planning and forecasting, and promotion effectiveness, within the broader merchandising context of assortment, space, category management, and financial planning. As a Solution Principal, you will join a dynamic team dedicated to expanding RELEX's footprint in retail merchandising. This role is fully remote.
We are hiring for industry background first. The strongest candidates have done this work inside a retailer and know the daily reality of the people we sell to: the weekly price review, the promotion that missed its forecast, the vendor funding conversation, the category reset that ran late. We can teach our platform and our sales process. We cannot teach what it is like to own a category or a price file.
Join us as a Presales Solution Principal and this is some of what you'll be doing:
Apply your hands-on pricing, promotions, and merchandising experience to conduct discovery, develop a RELEX point of view, lead workshops, and drive innovation with RELEX prospects
Apply deep RELEX solution expertise and industry knowledge to build tailored demonstrations of pricing and promotion capabilities using prospect data and scenarios
Provide thought leadership and work with pricing, and category leadership and their teams to align their pricing and promotional strategy, and build a strong business case supported by a compelling value proposition for deploying RELEX
Understand a prospect's needs through discovery sessions, then assemble a demonstration of what a RELEX solution would look like if implemented
Assist in creating Proofs of Concept and influence approach and configuration when necessary
Collaborate with internal functional groups including Professional Services, Central Presales, Product Strategy, Product Management, and Product Marketing
Interact with clients and present to prospect audiences, from category manager to C-suite
Develop and customize sales material, value narratives, and ROI models for pricing and promotion opportunities

7+ years in an operating role inside a retailer, grocer, or similar.
NOTE: We want people who have carried a category, a price file, or a promotional calendar as their day job, for example (non-exhaustive):
Category Manager, Category Merchant, or Buyer, owning assortment, margin, vendor negotiations, and promotional plans for a category
Pricing Manager, Pricing Analyst, or Director of Pricing, owning price strategy, rules, zones, and competitive response
Promotions Manager or Trade/Promotional Planner, owning the promotion calendar, forecasting, funding, and post-event measurement
Direct experience with the rhythms and tools of that work: the weekly and seasonal planning cadence, the spreadsheets and legacy systems people actually use, the trade-offs between margin, volume, price image, and inventory, and what it takes to get a price or promotion decision approved internally
Detailed knowledge of pricing and promotion business logic, such as price optimization and rule frameworks, price elasticity and demand modeling, price zones and family/link rules, KVI and price image management, competitor price response, promotional lift and cannibalization, and post-event effectiveness analysis
Working knowledge of the surrounding merchandising landscape: assortment planning, space planning, category management, vendor funding and trade spend, and merchandise financial planning
Understanding of how pricing and promotion decisions land downstream in forecasting and replenishment, and what goes wrong operationally when that handoff breaks
Consulting or presales experience in pricing, promotions, or merchandising software is valuable, but does not replace time spent in an operating role
Ability to see the bigger picture, translating customer issues into RELEX based solutions
Familiarity with the pricing, promotions, and merchandising technology landscape, and hands-on experience working with those solution providers as a user, evaluator, or implementation participant. You should be comfortable discussing how these systems work, where they fit in a merchandising tech stack, and what separates them
Analytical approach, with the confidence to discuss model logic, elasticities, and measurement methodology with both analysts and executives
Presentation skills
Knowledge, or desire to learn, of industry and sectors
Flexible and adaptable approach, being able to communicate advanced logic to a broad audience
Willingness to work within ambiguity and drive improvement, both for customers and our internal approach and resource
Comfort with travel across the US and Canada when needed, approx. 40%

Every RELEX implementation is a solution built from scratch for one customer: their processes, their data, their targets. (Senior) Supply Chain Consultants shape both sides of that build — the business processes and KPIs the customer will run on, and the configuration that makes them work in the system. Depending on your background you will lean more towards one side than the other. This is a heavily customer-facing role.
What you'll be doing
Understand how the customer really plans. Prepare, facilitate and document workshops to gather and specify business requirements, and run the data analysis that shows where the strengths and the gaps actually are.
Design the target picture — planning processes, roles and the KPIs the project is measured on — and guide customers towards RELEX best practice, including where their current way of working needs to change.
Build it. Configuration, business rules, workflows and reporting that deliver the design you just agreed, and that hold up in operation: nightly run performance, scalability and maintainability, not just functional correctness.
Make the value case tangible for customer leadership: define how forecast accuracy, availability, inventory and cost will be measured, and report honestly on where we stand.
Take it live. Coordinate User Acceptance Testing, resolve what testing surfaces, and upskill super users so the customer is proficient and self-sustaining after go-live.
Own adoption, not just delivery. A technically correct solution that nobody uses is not a successful project.
Document what you built — requirements, scope and configuration — so the project team, the customer and our Continuous Services colleagues can work with it after handover.
Work across disciplines : with Technical Consultants on the data model, interfaces and the customer's ERP landscape, and with Project Managers on scope, effort and timelines.
