Bridging the gap between operational practice and software systems by building operationally disciplined solutions.
Defining architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics across squads to ensure reliability and data integrity.
Collaborating with business and operational stakeholders to translate operational requirements into engineering solutions.
Hiring, mentoring and developing engineering managers and senior engineers to support team growth up to 30+ members.

At least 5 years of experience managing managers - leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, rather than running a single team.

Fintech or regulated-industry experience, with an understanding of the operational stakes of device management in a payments environment.

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably.

We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products.

From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

We're looking for a Senior Inventory Planner to own product launch planning and post-launch replenishment execution for Quince's UK and EU expansion. This is not a steady-state replen role. It's the planner who decides how deep we go on new products at launch, then operates the day-to-day to make sure those products actually land on time and scale well.
You'll size initial launch buys for products dropping into the UK and EU at a weekly cadence, often with little or no local demand history, by triangulating from Quince overall performance, comparable products, comparable markets, lead-time realities, and informed judgement.

Once products are live, you'll act on early sell-through signals and trigger replenishment decisions fast, pulling forward, doubling down on winners, cutting losses on losers, and adjusting the next launch wave based on what the market is teaching us.
This role sits at the heart of Quince's International expansion. Working alongside a planning and automation counterpart who owns the underlying forecasting models and demand sensing, you'll be the operator who turns those signals into real-world action.

Sizing the buys, placing the POs, working the relationships, and getting product in the warehouse on time. Your edge is judgement, speed, and the trust you build with the people who make execution actually happen.

You'll be operating where the tooling is still being built around you, the data is thinner than you'd like, and the answer often has to be reasoned from first principles. Comfort operating in a dynamic environment isn't a nice-to-have, it's the job.
The ideal candidate has lived this work before. Sizing launch buys, executing replenishment decisions, working POs through to landing at a DTC or M2C that moves quickly and has international exposure. You're a builder of relationships first and a builder of spreadsheets second.

You're energized by placing well-reasoned bets under uncertainty, by getting product to land on time when it shouldn't have, and by the trust you accumulate with vendors and cross-functional partners over time. You communicate constraints bluntly but constructively.

You don't wait for perfect data, and you don't let a winning product sit understocked while you wait for statistical significance.
Success in This Role Means
Product launch buys are sized well. Products that are market winners aren't crippled by stockouts and losers don't tie up working capital you can't recover.
Post-launch product replenishment decisions are fast and well judged. Safety stock and WOS is controlled and refreshed as market signals mature. Winning products scale into demand, losing products get cut before they bleed.
Forecast accuracy improves measurably on new products, even where historical data is thin.
POs land on time, in full, and any deviation is known, flagged, and managed proactively
Merch, sourcing, production partners, vendors, and your peer planners in other geographies trust you completely. You're the person they pick up the phone for, the one whose word on a PO they take to the bank, the one they share early intelligence with.
Inventory turns improve as the UK and EU business scales
The launch and replen frameworks you build for the UK don't just serve the UK today. They become the blueprint for how Quince plans every new market launch that comes next.

Own end-to-end launch planning for new products entering the UK and EU markets. Size the initial buy, sequence against lead times and launch dates, and translate it into clean PO recommendations
Take forecasting models, demand signals, and algorithmic recommendations developed by the team and operationalize them. Apply judgement on top, raise issues when the model is wrong, and feed real-world execution learnings back to improve the models
Manage POs end-to-end. Generate, adjust, expedite, and follow up with vendors and internal stakeholders to ensure on-time, in-full delivery against launch dates
Partner closely with merchandising on assortment and launch calendars, and with sourcing and production on lead times, capacity, vendor allocation, and PO execution. These are your primary day-to-day partners
Build and nurture strong working relationships with partners directly. Communicate constraints clearly, hold them accountable to commitments, escalate constructively when needed, and become the partner they prioritize when capacity is tight
Work as part of a global planning community. Share intelligence with planning counterparts in the US and other geographies, lift and adapt their analogs and learnings into UK and EU plans, and escalate cross-market issues quickly
Build and maintain the operational artifacts (trackers, dashboards, status notes) that give the rest of the business confidence in launch readiness and post-launch performance

The Senior Analyst, Outbound Logistics is a strategic, high-ownership role responsible for managing HelloFresh Canada's carrier network across both last mile and middle mile. You will serve as the primary point of contact for all carrier relationships — from onboarding new partners to holding the existing network accountable for quality and cost performance.
While the Systems and Analytics teams provide the tools and data, you are the operator who turns insight into action: renegotiating rates, escalating service failures, shaping network strategy, and continuously raising the bar on what "great" looks like for Canadian logistics.

s.t:

Own day-to-day and strategic relationships with last mile and middle mile carriers across the Canadian network
Hold carriers accountable to agreed KPIs, with a focus on On-Time Performance (OTP) and Contactless Completion (CC) error rates
Lead regular business reviews, issue escalations, and corrective action plans with carrier partners
Onboarding & Network Expansion
Lead end-to-end onboarding of new carrier partners, including operational setup, system integration, and readiness validation
Identify network gaps and proactively source, evaluate, and onboard partners to fill them
Cost Strategy & Optimization
Own carrier cost performance across the network; develop and execute a roadmap to continuously reduce cost per shipment without compromising service quality
Lead rate negotiations and contract renewals; benchmark carrier pricing against market and identify savings opportunities
Partner with Finance and Analytics to model cost scenarios and quantify the impact of network changes
Quality & Continuous Improvement
Monitor OTP, CC errors, and other service metrics; identify root causes and drive resolution with carriers
Develop and maintain scorecards and reporting frameworks that create transparency and drive accountability
Champion a culture of continuous improvement across the carrier base
Network Strategy
Contribute to the long-term logistics network strategy for Canada, including carrier diversification, regional coverage, and resilience planning
Translate business growth plans into network requirements; proactively adjust carrier mix and capacity to stay ahead of demand
Cross-functional Collaboration
Partner with Systems, Analytics, Customer Experience, and Operations teams to align carrier performance with broader business goals
Act as the voice of the carrier network internally, surfacing risks, opportunities, and trade-offs to leadership

s.h: Sound a-peeling? Here's what we're looking for
s.t:
3–5 years of experience in Logistics, Supply Chain, or Operations, with a focus on carrier management, partner onboarding, and network optimization
Demonstrated experience managing carriers against performance KPIs (OTP, damage rates, service failures) and leading corrective action processes
Strong commercial acumen — comfortable with rate negotiations, contract management, and cost modelling
Advanced proficiency in Excel and/or Google Sheets; able to build and manage performance scorecards, cost trackers, and cross-referenced datasets independently
Experience working with Transportation Management Systems (TMS) and routing or logistics platforms
Analytical mindset — able to identify trends in carrier performance data and translate them into clear action plans
Excellent stakeholder management skills; comfortable holding external partners accountable while maintaining productive working relationships
Highly organized and detail-oriented, with low error tolerance when managing carrier data, service areas, and network configurations
Ability to work autonomously, manage multiple priorities, and drive projects forward without a dedicated team
Experience in e-commerce, meal kit, or high-volume B2C logistics is an asset

The role will report into the Head of Procurement, within the finance function.
The Procurement Manager will lead sourcing, negotiation, and contracting activities across IT, Marketing, and General Procurement categories, acting as a business partner to internal stakeholders. This role owns the end-to-end procurement activities — from market analysis and supplier selection through negotiation, contracting, and ongoing supplier relationship management — with the goal of delivering cost savings, managing risk, and ensuring reliable, high-quality suppliers to the business.
The successful candidate will combine strong commercial and negotiation skills with the ability to build credibility and influence across a range of stakeholder groups.
The ideal candidate is proactive and confident, working independently to align procurement workload with business objectives.

Sourcing Strategy
Develop and execute sourcing strategies for IT (hardware, software, cloud, managed services), Marketing (agencies, media, creative production, digital, events, market research), and general/indirect spend categories, aligned to business objectives.
Conduct spend analysis, market research, and supplier landscape assessments to identify sourcing opportunities, cost-saving initiatives, and risk areas.
Plan and lead competitive sourcing events (RFI/RFP/RFQ), tendering, and supplier evaluation and selection processes.
Build and maintain rolling category plans that reflect business demand, budget cycles, and market developments.
Negotiation & Contracting
Lead commercial negotiations on pricing, terms, service levels, and contractual conditions to secure best value and minimise risk.
Partner with Legal to draft contracts and amendments, ensuring compliance with organisational policy and regulatory requirements.
Own contract renewal timelines, ensuring proactive re-negotiation ahead of expiry and avoiding lapses in critical supply.
Stakeholder Management
Act as a primary procurement point of contact for IT, Marketing, and other business stakeholders, translating business requirements into effective sourcing strategies.
Partner with stakeholders to define demand, scope requirements, and align sourcing timelines with project and budget cycles.
Provide regular updates and reports to stakeholders and leadership.
Influence and educate stakeholders on procurement best practices, policy, and governance requirements.
Supplier Relationship Management
Manage the end-to-end supplier lifecycle: onboarding, performance monitoring, risk management, and offboarding.
Establish and track supplier performance metrics (SLAs, KPIs) and lead regular business reviews with key suppliers.
Identify and resolve supplier performance issues, driving corrective action and continuous improvement plans.
Build strong, collaborative relationships with strategic suppliers to unlock innovation and long-term value.
Governance, Risk & Reporting
Ensure all sourcing and contracting activity complies with procurement policy, financial controls, and legal/regulatory standards.
Maintain accurate records of contracts, spend, and savings within procurement systems.
Report on workload performance, savings delivery, and risk exposure to procurement leadership.
Support audits and due diligence related to supplier risk, data security, and compliance (particularly relevant for IT and data-related categories).

5+ years of procurement lifecycle experience, ideally with exposure to IT and Marketing categories.
Demonstrated experience leading end-to-end sourcing events and negotiating complex commercial contracts.
Strong understanding of IT categories (software licensing, cloud/SaaS, hardware, telecom) and/or Marketing categories (agency, media, digital, production).
Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to engage confidently with senior leaders.
Strong analytical skills, with experience in spend analysis, market research, and savings tracking.
Solid understanding of contract law fundamentals and commercial terms (SLAs, KPIs, liability, IP, data protection clauses).
Proficiency with procurement/e-sourcing systems (e.g., Coupa, Netsuite, Omnea, Zip) and Microsoft Excel.
A can-do attitude and a curiosity to question, challenge, and improve working practices
Professional certification (e.g., CIPS, CPSM) preferred but not essential.
We don’t expect you to meet every requirement. If you’re excited by this role, we encourage you to apply.

We are seeking a driven and analytical Supply Chain Enablement Associate Manager to support the transformation of our ingredients and packaging inbound supply chain.

Reporting to the Associate Director, Supply Chain Enablement, you will lead standalone supply chain process and technology improvement workstreams end-to-end — turning operational signals into data-driven cases and delivering measurable impact.

As a part of the Procurement team, you will develop deep expertise in our processes, data, and technology, building the analytical foundation that drives continuous improvement across our E2E supply chain.
You will succeed in this role by combining structured analytical thinking, effective cross-functional collaboration, and strong project management skills to independently own and deliver workstreams from problem definition through implementation.

s.h: Lettuce share what this role will be responsible for
s.t:
Lead standalone supply chain process and technology improvement workstreams end-to-end, from opportunity identification and root cause analysis through implementation and adoption
Build data-driven analytical cases — quantify opportunity size and impact, assess root causes, and make clear recommendations to fix, standardize, or escalate
Run deep current- and future-state process mapping to isolate root causes; independently lead root cause and corrective action (RCCA) on workstream-level problems
Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders across the organization (including teams from procurement, planning, logistics, technology, data, fulfillment operations, and finance) to align on solutions and drive workstream-level change
Serve as the primary mentor and quality gate for offshore resources within your workstream — vetting new workstreams, defining execution plans, auditing quality, and managing SLA variances
Contribute to our source-to-pay technology and process knowledge; support master data and technology initiatives within your workstream scope
Maintain and improve standard operating procedures and documentation for workstream processes
Manage project plans, Jira workflows, and timelines; provide stakeholder updates and collaborate with our data team to track KPIs and report on progress

s.h: Sound a-peeling? Here's what we're looking for
s.t:
Bachelor's and/or Graduate degree in Business Management, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or equivalent field
4+ years of relevant consulting or industry experience with logistics, supply chain management, operations, or a related field
Demonstrated ability to build analytical cases — quantifying impact, sizing opportunities, and translating data into clear, actionable recommendations
Experience leading process improvement projects end-to-end, including stakeholder alignment, change communication, and post-implementation tracking
Working knowledge of Lean methodologies and root cause analysis tools (e.g., 5 Whys, Variable Tree Analysis); Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification is a plus
Proficiency in data analysis and visualization tools (e.g., Google Sheets, Tableau, Looker); ability to build or contribute to reporting dashboards
Subject matter knowledge in one or more of: procure-to-pay, source-to-pay, process mapping, spend analysis, or performance metrics
Demonstrated ability to collaborate across cross-functional teams and engage stakeholders at multiple levels of the organization
Clear and structured communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information and present recommendations to cross-functional audiences
Comfort operating in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment with the ability to self-direct a workstream with limited guidance

As a Junior Supply Chain Coordinator , you'll help ensure our production always receives the right ingredients and materials on time, in full, and with the required quality. You'll be the main point of contact for suppliers whenever deliveries don't go as planned and work closely with internal teams to find quick and effective solutions.
This role combines communication, coordination, and data analysis. You'll investigate issues, identify root causes, and support continuous process improvements. Your work has a direct impact on ensuring our customers receive their HelloFresh boxes exactly as expected.

Monitor inbound deliveries and ensure production is supplied on time.
Act as the main point of contact for suppliers regarding delivery delays, shortages, or quality deviations.
Lead confident and solution-oriented conversations with suppliers, following up until issues are resolved.
Collaborate closely with Procurement, Production, Warehouse, FSQA, and Operations teams.
Analyse delivery issues and perform root cause analyses to identify improvement opportunities.
Prepare reports and communicate insights clearly to internal stakeholders.
Support continuous improvement initiatives across our supply chain processes.
Help reduce food waste while maintaining excellent supplier performance and service levels.

A degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field, or an equivalent qualification.
First practical experience through internships, working student positions, or an entry-level role in Supply Chain, Logistics, or Manufacturing is a plus
Fluency in both French and English (minimum B2 level) , as you'll communicate daily with suppliers and internal stakeholders in both languages.
Strong communication skills and the confidence to manage challenging supplier conversations professionally and assertively.
A structured way of working with the ability to prioritise tasks and stay calm under pressure.
An analytical mindset with experience using Excel or Google Sheets. Experience with ERP, WMS, or BI tools is an advantage.
Good to know
The days off are Monday and Sunday.
This is a fully onsite position at our production site. Remote work is not available for this role.
Flexibility to work weekends when required is essential.

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.
As a Supply Chain Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to be a part of a multidisciplinary team that is responsible for sourcing and procuring parts over the world, managing supplier relationships and finding opportunities to reduce costs where possible, and the delivery of critical hardware to support space systems and launch products.

As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally
Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges
Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates
Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events

Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results.
Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate program in an engineering discipline, Supply Chain, Business Administration, or Operation Management and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship.
GPA of 3.0 or above.
3+ months of corporate function experience within the areas of supply chain.

6+ months of corporate function experience within the areas of supply chain.
Knowledge of the 5S principles
Experience with SQL and/or PowerBI
Proficient in Excel

Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027

It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace.

We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

s.h: FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY
s.t:

Learn more about ITAR here .
Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.
Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com. This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

s.h: FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY
s.t:
For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.
Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality. s.h: SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, SUPPLY CHAIN (LAUNCH SITE)
s.t:
SpaceX demands a new type of supply chain. We require our suppliers to provide premium quality with rapidly evolving designs at increasingly ambitious volumes. We are actively looking for candidates who possess comprehensive knowledge of manufacturing and quality tools and have an unrelenting motivation to enable suppliers to succeed.

This position will be the key focal point for Launch, supporting our Dragon and Falcon programs, and requires a combination of proven leadership and technical capabilities.
This is a highly technical position that requires practical experience in process engineering and new product development through stabilized production for the machined components and assemblies used in rockets and rocket engines. The ideal candidate will have a broad understanding of the machining and assembly of metallic components and associated processes, with the desire and capability to take on new challenges in unfamiliar areas to help enable our mission to Mars.

Act as the technical point of contact for assigned parts or systems within flight, non-flight, and launch site and recovery infrastructure, solving emergent challenges at suppliers and mitigating risk to the manifest by addressing high-impact manufacturing and quality challenges
Lead and coordinate containment activities to mitigate risk to build and launch schedules, and drive ongoing reliability improvements
Intervene and drive resolution at the supplier for critical path components to ensure zero disruption to the build schedule
Review issues on assigned parts and solve to the root cause, implementing changes at the supplier, at SpaceX, or both, as appropriate, drive further actions to closure, and re-source to new suppliers where appropriate
Create and disposition issue tickets where needed, working with engineering counterparts to implement, but not limited to, required re-work, repair, or use as-is disposition
Become thoroughly familiar with your assigned parts, systems, and the processes that make up the overall assembly, and become the primary point of contact for supply chain-related defects on your parts
Work with procurement to find exceptional suppliers and vet them appropriately for quality and ability to meet our aggressive takt times
Conduct design for manufacturing (DFM) reviews to ensure parts are manufacturable at early stages, preferably prior to sourcing
Own the new product introduction (NPI) process at a supplier for new parts, drawing changes, or when re-sourcing existing parts to a new supplier
Drive the production part approval process (PPAP) program to ensure stable supply, reduce inspection oversight, and improve overall delivery time
Demonstrate innovation, technical excellence, attention to detail, self-direction, and courage to push the technical envelope, which is conventionally held in the industry
Drive for results and customer satisfaction by collaborating with teams, leading projects, and continuously driving improvement in the supply base

The Health, Safety and Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for supporting the implementation of Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) programs while ensuring efficient procurement, inventory control, supplier coordination, and supply chain processes. The role assists in maintaining compliance with company policies, regulatory requirements, and management systems while supporting uninterrupted laboratory and operational activities through effective resource planning and supply management.

Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Environmental Science, Occupational Safety and Health, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Chemistry, or any related field.
Experience
At least 1-3 years of experience in HSE, procurement, supply chain, inventory management, or related functions.
Experience in laboratory, industrial, or service environments is an advantage.
Experience/Technical Knowledge

Inventory planning and demand forecasting
Stock optimization and working capital control
Supplier coordination and risk management
Proven ability to manage and improve inventory KPIs (months cover, obsolescence, expiry, wastage, stock-outs).
Working knowledge of HSE requirements in laboratory or industrial settings, including chemical handling, waste management, and workplace safety.
Training or certification related to ISO 14001 / ISO 45001, or equivalent HSE systems, is an advantage.
Experience supporting or implementing Health and Safety programs, inspections, risk assessments, and incident investigations.
Experience working cross-functionally with Operations, Finance, QA, and Procurement.
Skills & Competencies
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to influence and coach teams without direct authority.
Detail-oriented, disciplined, and able to manage competing priorities.
Proficient in MS Office and basic data analysis tools.
Strong written and spoken English; Filipino proficiency preferred.
Language
Proficient in English & Filipino (both written and verbal).
